mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding six months raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the average 60-day return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% and remains there for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 2% signals a monetary policy tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed thresholds, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals broad-based demand weakness, which erodes corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (±0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as improving retail demand signals near-term corporate earnings strength.
failure_condition: The correlation between month-over-month change in RSAFS and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
